concept.reason: Actual whole specimen photo and primary head/fin photos plus diagnosed ratios suffice for bounded reconstruction. No extra generated concept; output fourviews are inspection plans, not four originalphotos.

original_scope.en: Planned animal asset: exceptionally slender needlelike rostrum tapering from a large eye.

evidence_anchors.whole_body: Daderot2011 real ROM specimen photo, CC0,4320x2179. Long needlelike jaws, large postrostral orbital region, long trunk/tail and paddle bones visible. Specimen accession not visible inphoto, so NOT asserted to be VP47698. Postmortem bend, missing/overlapping bones and matrix outline not living contour.
evidence_anchors.head_and_fins: McGowan1989 pp414–415 Fig1A and2A genuine photographs of OUM J10305, with author assessment p420: almost complete, no grounds to question authenticity, partial forefins and hindfin. These validate long matching upper/lower jaws, round orbit, forefin architecture. Different individual from ROM photo, not merged as single specimen measurements.
evidence_anchors.scale: Paul, Princeton Field Guide to Mesozoic Sea Reptiles public size supplement, p3: L.tenuirostris ROM VP47698 estimated TL2.56m, estimated mass55kg. Use TL only as representative same-species scale; NOT museum-photo measurement or confirmed shared accession.
evidence_anchors.taxonomy: 2025 Pratas e Sousa et al. APP70:179–192 discussion retains L.tenuirostris and distinguishes its long slender snout from short-snouted L.moorei. McGowan1989 old name Leptopterygius tenuirostris is used only as historical same-species research. Swiss NMO26575 and other Hauffiopteryx material excluded.
evidence_anchors.period: Lower Jurassic England; ROM caption Lyme Regis. No exact ammonite zone asserted for unnumbered photo.

scale.status: published representative estimate, not scan/caliper total
scale.reason: Only total2.56m is a published specimen-based length estimate. Other values are bounded original modeling proportions, not measurements of VP47698. McGowan ratios use jaw length: snout>0.70, orbit<0.25 (often<0.20); OUM J10305 snout ratio0.72 and prenarial0.60, with9mm tip ambiguity. Large eye means large relative to short posterior head, NOT giant relative to entire long skull.

morphology: Core: exceptionally long fine needlelike rostrum tapering from large orbital region; equally slender lower jaw extends almost to upper tip. Keep both jaws thin and continuous with skull. No Eurhinosaurus half-length lower jaw or swordfish horn.
Head rear is short; rounded bony orbit dominates postrostral head but occupies less than one quarter jaw length. External living eye is smaller than orbit, not exposed bony ring or oversized eyeball.
Long slender trunk and elongated flexible tailstock, not deep tuna body. Neutral nearly horizontal swimming; do not copy severe postmortem curve in ROM slab.

Exactly four attached paddles. Forepair longer and broader than hindpair, tapered distal ends enclosing digits. McGowan forefin4primarydigits and hindfin3 are internal anatomy only; no exposed toes or skeleton.

Tail axis is shallowly downturned or approximately straight: McGowan1989 wedge-shaped centra confirm a weak flexure, not an acute downturned crescent. Keep a long tapering lower axial tail and a modest inferred upper caudal membrane, verticalplane. No steep V-shaped bonebend, large symmetric shark crescent, or horizontal whale fluke.

Dorsal fin, caudal membrane margins, skin thickness and pigmentation are conservative ichthyosaur soft-tissue inferences, not preserved outlines in the selected sources. Use low modest dorsalfin, shallow tail not dramatic sail.
Closed or nearly closed jaws with subtle mouth seam; small slender teeth optional/subdued, no sabertooth fangs. Slight overbite at most, not genus-defining extreme overbite.
Small lateral nares ahead ofeyes; no dolphin blowhole, gills, scales, armor, ribs, slab, label or museum frame.
uncertainty: No four-angle realphoto set. Whole specimen plus real head and fin photographs, explicit anatomical ratios, and published estimate support bounded3D reconstruction, not photogrammetry.
The ROM photo accession is not verified. Scale VP47698 and shape photo are same-species separate evidence, never represented as one measured individual.
Museum mounts and historical material may be restored; OUM J10305 assessment is specifically favorable, while R498 and BGS51236 are not adopted as exact geometric anchors.
Dorsal/caudal softfin outlines and bodywidth are unpreserved. Weak tailflexure is required; generic steep lunar tail unsupported.
Do not use infant CAMSM J35178 proportions from Lomax2012 as adult head/body ratio; paper used for species diagnosis/context only.
palette: Restrained muted grey-blue with lighter underside as artistic convention, no claim of preserved pattern.
acceptance_focus: Front lateral: paired thin long jaws, large posterior orbitalregion and short cheek, elongated body and shallow tail.
Side head-on and top: fine tapering snout and exactly four paddles, broadbases blend into trunk, no detached spike.
Perspective: living smooth continuous body, no fossil bones; weakflexure and restrained fin outlines.
Species and scale citations preserve material distinctions, dimensions inferred beyond nominal2.56m. ScientificQA independent of template validation.
